events.title: The Village: Sites, Stories, & Synagogues Walking Tour
events.description: The Lower East Side Jewish Conservancy hosts a tour of the often-overlooked Jewish history of Greenwich Village, which stretches back more than 200 years. Stops include Congregation Darech Amuno, housed in a 150-year-old converted townhouse and in the Village since 1838; one of the oldest Jewish cemeteries in the country, hidden in plain sight on West 11th Street; and an early home of Temple Emanu-El in a converted Baptist Church on East 12th Street. The walk also traces the many Jewish musicians, artists, and activists who shaped the neighborhood alongside figures like Dylan, Springsteen, Hendrix, and Ginsberg.

organizer.organizer: The Lower East Side Jewish Conservancy (LESJC)
organizer.description: The Lower East Side Jewish Conservancy (LESJC) is an educational non-profit, created in 1998, to preserve and support the Lower East Side’s community of living synagogues and other historic structures, and to raise public awareness of the neighborhoods distinct cultural identity. As the birthplace of American Jewish civilization, and the most iconic immigrant neighborhood in America, we share this history by taking people on walking tours which enter sacred sites, where you learn how past generations came here, lived and worshiped. Learn more about LESJC here.

events.title: Navigating the Fall 2026 NYC Art Scene
events.description: The Community Scholar Program hosts artist Tobi Kahn for a virtual tour of New York City gallery exhibitions in Fall 2026. Participants visit multiple galleries, hear from curators and art historians, and are introduced to new artists and contemporary works. The tour is designed to sharpen the eye and deepen appreciation of what is current in the art world.

organizer.description: Spinoza Havurah is an international, spiritually oriented, Humanistic Jewish online-only community. Our leaders are in the US and the UK, but our members and attendees are from around the world.

events.title: Jewish Germany Part 3: Virtual Jewish Bavaria Tour
events.description: Qesher presents a virtual tour of the Jewish history of Bavaria through Regensburg, Bamberg, Nuremberg, and Munich. Stops include Regensburg’s medieval Jewish quarter and New Synagogue, Bamberg’s historic Judengasse, Munich’s Ohel Jakob Synagogue and memorials to sites lost during Kristallnacht, and Nuremberg’s medieval Jewish quarter and destroyed synagogue. The tour also traces Nuremberg’s history as a center of Jewish scholarship that later became a hub of Nazi propaganda, along with postwar efforts to restore Jewish life.

organizer.description: There are Jewish communities all around the globe with their own unique history, culture, places, and most of all, people and stories. All of them different, but sharing so much. The aim of Qesher is to connect these different Jewish traditions, not just to know of each other, but to learn about each other. We believe that there is great value in creating a deeper understanding within the Jewish world and exploring Jewish experiences and identities in all their diversity.

events.title: The Sound of Resistance: A Conversation with Author Heather Morris
events.description:
Heather Morris’s 2018 novel, “The Tattooist of Auschwitz” became an instant bestseller after it was published. Now, Morris returns with a new novel showcasing the astonishing bravery of ordinary people in extraordinary times.

In “The Pianist of Montparnasse,” Morris tells the story of 11-year-old Josephine and the teacher who risked everything for her. When Josephine’s mother and brother are arrested by the Nazis, her mother orders her to go to the only person she can trust: her piano teacher, Andrée Levallois. What Josie does not know is that her teacher and her parents are part of the French Resistance. Andrée and her parents take the child in, risking everything to keep her safe. But the stakes grow higher as their operations become more dangerous, and the family’s strength of will and conviction are tested as they fight for the future they hope to see.

Please join us to meet Heather Morris and discuss the book on Sunday November 1, 2026, 6 pm ET, online.
Sign up below to participate. You’ll receive a reminder email with a Zoom link before the event begins.
About our speakers:
Heather Morris is a native of New Zealand, now residing in Australia. For several years, while working in a large public hospital in Melbourne, she studied and wrote screenplays. In 2003, she was introduced to a gentleman who had “a story worth telling,” which formed the basis of her first novel, The Tattooist of Auschwitz, and its follow-up, Cilka’s Journey. Her third novel, Three Sisters, concluded the Tattooist trilogy. One of the twenty-first century’s best-selling books, The Tattooist of Auschwitz was made into an acclaimed miniseries in 2024. Heather’s books have sold more than nineteen million copies worldwide.
Heather will be in conversation with Rebecca Phillips, publisher of 70 Faces Media. 70 Faces Media is the organization behind six of the Jewish world’s most beloved and longstanding digital brands: JTA, My Jewish Learning, Kveller, The Nosher, Hey Alma, and the New York Jewish Week.
This conversation with Heather Morris is presented by Blackstone Publishing, our sponsor for the event.

organizer.description: Whether you grew up observing Shabbat every Friday night, or had your first taste of matzah ball soup when you married into a Jewish family, there’s no one way to parent Jewish kids. Kveller is here to give you ideas you can run with–ideas for first-time parents, interfaith parents, queer parents, adoptive parents, and everything in between–with the hopes that you can find information and inspiration that is right for your family.

events.title: Oppenheimer: Beyond the Bomb
events.description: The Florence Melton School of Adult Jewish Learning hosts author and journalist David Rieff for a conversation about his new biography, “Robert Oppenheimer: The Sphinx Without a Secret,” part of the Jewish Lives series. Rieff moves beyond the Manhattan Project to explore Oppenheimer’s inner life, from childhood trauma to his ambivalent relationship with his Jewish heritage and his lifelong devotion to scientific universalism. The session considers how the identities we inherit shape the individuals we become.

organizer.organizer: The Florence Melton School of Adult Jewish Learning

events.title: A New Heaven and a New Earth: How the Bible Cultivates Hope for the Future
events.description: The Jewish Theological Seminary of America presents a session examining biblical passages designed to cultivate hope and considering whether the Bible can serve as a resource for hope in today’s crisis-driven society. The discussion explores how scripture envisions a future and the ways it has shaped religious imagination of a new heaven and a new earth.

organizer.description: The Jewish Theological Seminary of America (JTS) is an educational institution of Conservative Judaism.

events.title: Iyun Programme, in Memory of Maureen Kendler z”l

Participants study the laws in depth with weekly chavruta preparation and textual skills are required. The program aims to raise the standard of women’s knowledge of Gemara and Halacha in the UK and beyond.

The sessions explore Noah’s behavior after the flood and the complex relationships of the Patriarchs and Matriarchs that shaped the formation of the Jewish people.

events.title: My Name is Stramer
events.description: The YIVO Institute for Jewish Research hosts author Mikołaj Łoziński in discussion with Irena Grudzińska Gross about the newly released English translation of his historical fiction novel “My Name is Stramer.” The novel follows the Stramer family in interwar Tarnów, where Nathan chases hare-brained schemes to support his wife Rywka and their six children as sinister forces begin to creep into their world. The program is co-sponsored by the Polish Cultural Institute New York, with additional support from the Ministry of Polish Culture and the Adam Mickiewicz Institute.

organizer.description: The YIVO Institute for Jewish Research is dedicated to the preservation and study of the history and culture of Eastern European Jewry and Yiddish language.

events.title: Truth on Trial: 80 Years After Nuremberg
events.description: The Center for Jewish History presents a conversation between historian Natalie Livingstone, author of “The Nuremberg Women,” and Israeli journalist Nadav Eyal on the Nuremberg Trials, justice after the Holocaust, and their legacy today, moderated by Gavriel Rosenfeld. Livingstone highlights the overlooked women — prosecutors, journalists, witnesses, and activists — who helped shape modern international justice, while Eyal turns to the present and the implications for Israel and Jewish communities worldwide. A book signing and light reception follow the program.

organizer.description: The Center for Jewish History is home to the largest collection for Jewish History and culture held outside of Israel, and offers a wide range of learning opportunities to the public.

events.title: The Pin That Slew the Serpent: Unearthing the Objects of the Talmud
events.description: The Community Scholar Program offers a course on everyday objects in the Talmudic text, from Hillel’s skylight to the hairpin of Rabbi Akiva’s daughter. While texts reflect the interests of the literate elite, objects such as furniture, clothes, and kitchenware open a window into the lives of the illiterate masses. The course explores how the rabbis used ordinary household items to respond to the concerns of society at large.

events.title: The Karaite Jews of Egypt: A Hidden Chapter in Jewish History
events.description: Qesher traces the lesser-known legacy of Karaite Jews in Egypt through the streets of Alexandria and the lecturer’s own family history. The session explores how Karaites differ from Rabbanite Jews in prayer, Torah interpretation, kashrut, and gender roles. The tradition continues to survive and evolve today in other parts of the globe.

events.title: The Heart of Jewish Ukraine: A Free Online Journey
events.description: The Online Jewish Travel Club presents a free online gathering with independent guide and lecturer Evgenia Kempinski on the diversity of Jewish life in the Pale of Settlement in Ukraine. The session explores the shtetls, each with its own traditions, along with the cultural and political centers of Odesa and Kyiv and the enlightened streets of Lviv and Brody. A recording is included.

events.title: The American Jewish Experience: A Reflection in this 250th Year of the US
events.description: Keeping It Sacred hosts Rabbi Heather Miller for an Election Day program reflecting on the American Jewish experience over the past 250 years. The session marks America’s 250th anniversary with an exploration of the history of Jewish life in the United States.

organizer.description: Keeping It Sacred is an international Reform Jewish community dedicated to creating accessible, relevant, and meaningful opportunities for connection, learning, and spiritual growth. Led by Rabbi Heather Miller, our participatory online programs bring people together across more than 12 time zones to explore Jewish wisdom, celebrate sacred moments, engage with today’s world, and build community. We welcome people of all backgrounds, identities, abilities, and levels of Jewish knowledge to come as they are, be seen and heard, ask questions, and find meaning in Jewish tradition and community.

events.title: Introduction to Bible with Rabbi Ephraim Buchwald
events.description: The National Jewish Outreach Program presents a course with Rabbi Buchwald offering a general overview of the content and style of the Bible, covering the Five Books of the Torah. The sessions review basic literary and theological approaches to Bible study, both traditional and modern, through analysis of the biblical text.

organizer.description: The National Jewish Outreach Program (NJOP) is an independent, non-profit organization dedicated to providing a basic Jewish education for every Jew in America.

events.title: More Than a Symbol: The Jewish Labor Bund in History
events.description: The YIVO Institute for Jewish Research hosts Joshua Meyers for a talk on the Jewish Labor Bund, drawing on the Bund Archive preserved at YIVO. The session traces the Bund’s history from its origins through World War II, when it served as the standard bearer of Diaspora Socialism in the Jewish communities of Eastern Europe, and examines its evolving relationships with Zionists, Communists, and other movements. The talk also considers the legacy of the Bund and of Diaspora Socialism in the 21st century.

organizer.description: The YIVO Institute for Jewish Research is dedicated to the preservation and study of the history and culture of Eastern European Jewry and Yiddish language.

events.title: Understanding Past Realities of the Holocaust: Photography Versus Art
events.description: The Holocaust and the United Nations Outreach Programme, the Fritz Ascher Society for Persecuted, Ostracized and Banned Art, and the Permanent Mission of Germany to the United Nations organize a discussion marking the November Pogrom of 1938, euphemistically called “Kristallnacht.” Historians Dr. Christoph Kreutzmüller and Dr. Rachel Perry examine how photography and art depicted the Nazi state-orchestrated campaign of terror perpetrated against Jewish men, women, and children across Germany, Austria, and the Sudetenland from November 9 to 10, 1938. The discussion considers what photography and art reveal about the lived realities of the victims and the broader society in which the violence was perpetrated.

organizer.description: Discussing and exhibiting artists who were persecuted, ostracized and banned by an authoritarian regime

events.title: Media Bias in the United States: The Catastrophic Failure of Modern Journalism
events.description: Chai Mitzvah hosts David, U.S. Media Research Manager at CAMERA, for a presentation on how media institutions have failed to deliver quality journalism in their coverage of Israel. Drawing on his work at the media monitoring organization, David examines how such failures have vilified victims, left perpetrators unaccountable, and distorted policy debates. This is Part 1 of CAMERA’s three-part series on media bias in the U.S., U.K., and Israel.

organizer.description: Chai Mitzvah’s goal is to strengthen communities by enhancing Jewish engagement. Through small group learning, individual spiritual/ritual growth, and opportunities for social action, participants grow Jewishly and engage more in their communities.

events.title: Melton Meets the Moment: Israel Vote — What Comes Next?
events.description: The Florence Melton School of Adult Jewish Learning hosts Rabbi Dr. Danny Schiff for a two-part follow-up to Ballots and Power analyzing the results of Israel’s October 27 Knesset election. The second turns to the U.S.-Israel relationship after the American midterm elections, considering how changes in American political leadership may affect Israel’s emerging government.

events.title: Tasting History: Recipes of Resilience with Alon Shaya and June Hersh
events.description:
In Memories of a Good Meal, multiple James Beard Award-winning chef Alon Shaya and acclaimed culinary historian June Hersh capture the extraordinary stories of ten Holocaust survivors and World War II heroes.

Inspired by Shaya’s work with the Rescued Recipes initiative and his deep friendship with the late survivor Steven Fenves, the authors traveled to interview survivors firsthand. They explored the powerful memories of food that remained with them throughout the decades, transforming those poignant recollections into recipes that can be passed down for generations.

Join us for a moving event with the authors on November 5 as they discuss their deeply personal commitment to preserving history through the lens of personal experience, resilience, and hope.
